newsitem.title: USA: Wall St seen resuming rally, tightening fears fade.
newsitem.headline: Wall St seen resuming rally, tightening fears fade.

text.p: Wall Street stocks are poised to resume their record climb and bonds bolted higher after a shockingly weak September payrolls eased fears that the Fed would raise short-term interest rates by year end.

Analysts cautioned that a closer look of the report showed a higher-than-expected rise in average hourly earnings and a longer work week. Thus the report did not rule out a near-term Fed tightening or provide enough fodder for Fed easing talk.
After surging nearly 1-1/2 points on the report, the long bond was up 27/32 to yield 6.77 percent.
That brought the yield to the lowest levels since August.

The December S&P 500 index futures contract rose 3.25 to 700.95, indicating the Dow might open up about 26 points. The Dow on Wednesday scored a record closing high of 5933.97 and slipped one point Thursday ahead of the key jobs report.

"News that the economy is slowing down in one-way good news for bonds," said Gail Dudack, chief investment strategist UBS Securities. "It also certainly creates a great opening for the stock market to move higher and validates what it's been doing. But the jury is still out on whether this ends up being good news for the stock market overall."

"If there are signs the economy is slowing, it validates (news from) companies that have been pre-releasing negative view for the quarter or 1997. So there's a double-edged sword for equities," she said.
"What it means for earnings is the real question. The market has to be driven by earnings at this juncture six years into the bull market," Dudack said.

Michael Metz, Oppenheimer and Co's chief investment strategist, said the report was not a totally "bullish picture but does take the steam out of the economy. Now the worry is if the economy is slowing down too much."
